guard_streams.source: Bulletin: BDUK delivery performance, quarterly: April 2025 to Sept 2025
guard_streams.write_limit: The release contains aggregate, revisable official statistics and geographic summaries; it cannot be transferred to selected parcels without an exact current join.

facts.detail: The release covers two quarters from 1 April to 30 September 2025.
BDUK published two quarters of data together after shortening its reporting lag.
The figures are designated official statistics.
Yorkshire and the Humber recorded 19 percent of England delivery, about 11,400 premises.
The South East recorded 18 percent, about 11,300 premises.
The North West recorded 17 percent, about 10,300 premises.
The report used BDUK management information as of 23 October 2025.
It used the July 2025 NSUL and May 2025 NSPL.
The Ofcom source was July 2024 Connected Nations data from the Summer Update 2024.
Historical time series were revised to reflect improved supplier reporting.

guard_streams.source: Bulletin: BDUK delivery performance, quarterly: April 2024 to December 2024
guard_streams.write_limit: This first historical quarterly release reports revised aggregate subsidy delivery and source versions; it cannot establish current selected-parcel coverage.

facts.detail: The bulletin was published on 24 July 2025.
The release covers delivery from 1 April to 31 December 2024.
It was the first release in BDUK's quarterly official-statistics series.
Previously reported financial-year values were reviewed and revised after supplier reporting improvements.
The report used BDUK management information as of 10 July 2025.
It used the April 2025 National Statistics UPRN Lookup.
It used the February 2025 National Statistics Postcode Lookup.
It used July 2024 Ofcom Connected Nations data from Summer Update 2024.
It used Ordnance Survey AddressBase Premium Epoch 117.
The release also presented total premises built under BDUK gigabit contracts.

guard_streams.source: Local Full Fibre Network programme evaluation plan
guard_streams.write_limit: An evaluation framework and programme theory cannot establish current serviceability or measured speed for selected parcels.

facts.detail: The LFFN evaluation plan was published on 15 August 2025.
The evaluation covers waves two and three of the Local Full Fibre Networks programme.
BDUK commissioned GC Insights, Belmana and Darren Kilburn.
LFFN was a £200 million programme.
The programme aimed to stimulate commercial investment in gigabit-capable connectivity.
The evaluation is organised into six work packages.
It aims to identify and value programme outcomes and impacts.
It examines the effectiveness of delivery models.
Lessons are intended to inform future infrastructure initiatives including Project Gigabit.
The plan notes that only two percent of UK premises had full-fibre access in 2016.
